defs.def: a person who is or was in the same class as you at school or college 同班同学

ex.s: Once in a lecture, the professor tried repeating my name after me over and over in front of thirty classmates.
ex.t: 有一次在课上，教授当着三十名同学的面，一遍又一遍地跟着我重复我的名字。

ex.s: I feared that my classmates might grow tired of my efforts or even lose patience with me.
ex.t: 我担心同学们可能会厌倦我的努力，甚至对我失去耐心。

ex.s: Many of my classmates got interested and came up to me after class.
ex.t: 我的许多同学产生了兴趣，课后围到我身边。

ex.s: Throughout our Junior year, my classmates and I have been worried about what colleges will see when they look at our whole life story reduced to a single 200-word essay.
ex.t: 整个高三那年，我和同学们一直担心，当大学招生官把我们整个生平浓缩成一篇200词的短文来审视时，他们会看到什么。

ex.s: She is unpopular with her classmates.
ex.t: 她和同学在一起很不受欢迎

ex.s: She searched the faces of her classmates for signs of panic.
ex.t: 当某事与他们的观点矛盾时，他们不会将其视为例外。

ex.s: However, while some of her classmates edged ahead, others actually fell behind.
ex.t: 然而，虽然她的一些同学逐渐领先，但其他人实际上落后了。

ex.s: To get the attention of her classmates.
ex.t: 为了引起同学们的注意。

ex.s: David had a brain disease which prevented him from walking or running like other children, but at school his classmates thought of him as a regular kid.
ex.t: David患有一种脑部疾病，使他无法像其他孩子一样走路或跑步，但在学校里同学们把他当作普通孩子看待。

ex.s: David had a brain disease which prevented him from walking or running like other children, but at school his classmates thought of him as a regular kid.
ex.t: David患有一种脑部疾病，使他无法像其他孩子一样走路或跑步，但在学校里同学们把他当作普通孩子看待。

ex.s: My classmates ranged from those kids with pale skin and large blue eyes to those with rich brown skin and dark hair.
ex.t: 我的同学从皮肤苍白、蓝眼睛的孩子到深棕色皮肤、黑头发的孩子都有。

ex.s: The author’s classmate.
ex.t: 作者的同学。

ex.s: Many students say they will talk to their friend or classmates because they're of the same age and can understand each other.
ex.t: 只有少数选择自己处理问题。

ex.s: Recent research suggests that if an argument gets resolved，the emotional response tied to it is significantly reduced or almost completely erased．Thus，it may be worth bringing up issues with your friends， family members，or classmates rather than holding them back．
ex.t: 最近的研究表明，如果一场争论得到解决，与之相关的情绪反应会显著减少，或几乎完全消除。因此，与其压抑，不如与朋友、家人或同学把问题提出来，可能最终会有更好的结果。

ex.s: “We found that the least well-liked teens had become more aggressive over time toward their classmates.
ex.t: "我们发现最不受欢迎的青少年随着时间的推移变得越来越具有攻击性。

ex.s: From now on, I started to play my football with classmates after school.
ex.t: 从那时起，我开始放学后和同学们一起踢足球。

ex.s: Through the years, I’d run into former students who would provide    51    on old classmates.
ex.t: 这些年来，我偶遇了一些以前的学生，他们会提供关于老同学的___51___信息。

ex.t: 这些年来，我偶遇了一些以前的学生，他们会提供关于老同学的___51___信息。

ex.s: He started to ask for help from his classmates and neighbours and persuaded them to donate money.
ex.t: 他开始向同学和邻居寻求帮助，并说服他们捐钱。

ex.s: Recommend one to your classmates.
ex.t: 向你的同学推荐一个。

ex.s: SELF-CONTROL Questionnaire 1 Do you ever lose your temper with your family, friends, or classmates?
ex.t: 自我控制问卷1您是否曾经对家人、朋友或同学发过脾气？

ex.s: On Monday, my classmate and I spoke about what we did at the weekend – it felt really strange not to already know what he had done.
ex.t: 周一，我和我的同学谈到了我们在周末所做的事情–不知道他做了什么感觉真的很奇怪。
